summary_long:
Overview:

Between July and September 2026, about 1.19 million people in 46 predominantly productive districts of Mozambique are in acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above), including roughly 81,000 in Emergency (IPC Phase 4) and 1.1 million in Crisis (IPC Phase 3). This is driven by flooding and Cyclone Gezani damaging crops, livestock, and seasonal food sources, prolonged heat limiting agricultural recovery and reducing pasture and water, conflict in Cabo Delgado and northern Nampula displacing over 27,000 people and disrupting markets and services, and persistently high staple prices alongside rising fuel/transport costs and inflation reducing purchasing power. Conditions are expected to worsen in the October 2026–March 2027 lean season, with around 1.84 million people likely in IPC Phase 3 or above and those in Phase 4 projected to more than triple to about 254,000, due to depleted household stocks, ongoing northern conflict, anticipated El Niño impacts in the south and center, and compounding shocks and displacement.

Recommendations:

Maintain humanitarian food assistance while strengthening resilience through agricultural production support, continued livelihood programmes, and targeted adaptation measures for anticipated El Niño impacts. Expand safe water access by increasing storage capacity amid expected below-normal rainfall, ensure agricultural and fisheries inputs are available in local markets, and intensify pest and disease monitoring with technical assistance for crops and livestock. Improve market access to enable the sale of agricultural surpluses and fisheries products.
summary_short: 1.19 million hungry, worsening to 1.84 million during lean season

summary_long: Ethiopia faces overlapping risks from armed conflict and political tensions across multiple regions, driving displacement, restricting access, and disrupting livelihoods. Severe climate shocks—drought in lowland areas and flooding elsewhere—combined with economic instability are worsening food insecurity and eroding household coping capacity. A fluid influx of refugees and asylum seekers, underfunded aid, and administrative and access constraints further strain host communities and hinder the humanitarian response.
summary_short: Conflict, climate shocks fuel displacement, hunger; underfunded aid hinders response
